findings.summary: Each model day integrates rates calculated for the previous model date, then applies current-day agromanagement, then calculates current-day rates. Timed management therefore affects current-day rates but not the integration that has already occurred on that date; state-triggered events inspect post-integration current states.

Within calc_rates water balance executes before SNOMIN; within integrate water balance executes before SNOMIN. SNOMIN therefore consumes water-flow/rate information under a fixed water-first ownership order.

Engine calculates crop rates before soil rates. Crop RNuptake demand is therefore computed from NAVAIL state integrated at the start of the day, then SNOMIN consumes that same day's RNuptake. This is an explicit one-way daily lag/explicit coupling contract: soil transformations calculated later cannot revise same-day crop demand.

Crop evapotranspiration calculates TRA/WTRALY before the soil water balance calculates its current-day rates; MLWB then uses published crop extraction as a prescribed sink. The next day's crop stress sees the integrated soil state. This is an explicit daily crop-first water-demand / soil-response coupling.

Timed amendment signals are dispatched before current-day calc_rates; SNOMIN collects amendment placeholders in that calc_rates and integrates them on the next Engine integration call. Calendar labels therefore describe the rate day, while state incorporation occurs at the following integration boundary.

On END_DATE the Timer emits OUTPUT and TERMINATE before Engine integrates that date. Engine then integrates the previous day's rates, processes management and current-day rates, saves output, and terminates. Thus final-day output is post-integration but current-day rates are not subsequently integrated. END_DATE is an integration boundary, not a fully executed additional rate day.

CROP_FINISH is deferred until after crop and soil calc_rates. A crop reaching maturity during integration can therefore still execute one final current-day crop calc_rates before finalize/delete; those newly calculated rates are not integrated when the crop is deleted. Final states remain correct for the integrated transition, but final-day rates should not be interpreted as realized fluxes.

A single daily state jump may cross multiple configured thresholds. Dispatcher evaluates thresholds independently, so all crossed rising thresholds should fire once; adversarial test added to guard this behavior.

Engine deletes crop state/rate registrations recursively and forces garbage collection because signal subscriptions otherwise retain objects. New crop start is rejected while a crop object remains. No additional rotation ownership defect was established in this tranche.

Multiple apply_n_snomin events on the same rate day append organic amendment pools but baseline mineral NH4/NO3 placeholders are assigned, so each later event overwrites mineral N from earlier events. Repair accumulates mineral-N contributions.

findings.summary: Rainfall and irrigation enter through distinct current-day inputs (drv.RAIN and RIRR) and are combined in infiltration/surface-water logic rather than overwriting one another. No duplicate-source defect established.

N translocatable donor pools are computed from pre-transition Namount and living biomass, while RNdeath for the same day independently claims N from that same pre-transition donor pool. Under sufficiently strong simultaneous senescence and translocation, RNdeath + RNtranslocation can exceed donor N available above zero, potentially driving organ N negative even though internal translocation itself algebraically cancels in the whole-crop balance. Repair must transactionally limit donor translocation after same-day N death/residual ownership.

findings.summary: Crop root depth RD is integrated before soil integration. MLWB then updates layer rooting weights to the new RD during soil integrate. Current-day crop ET and SNOMIN rates are subsequently calculated using that same new RD/root geometry. No one-day disagreement between water and N access was found at root-layer crossing; both see post-integration RD on the rate day.

Root depth growth is stopped only when FR equals exactly zero, not when actual root dry-matter growth is zero. The source documents this as an intentional legacy WOFOST modelling choice rather than an implementation accident.

On crop start, Engine creates the crop during AgroManager and immediately calculates crop rates on the start date; those rates are integrated at the next boundary. At maturity/harvest, the transition reaching finish is integrated first, then one additional set of crop rates may be calculated before finalize/delete but is never integrated. First and last calendar-labelled rate days are therefore not symmetric.

Because finish is deferred until after calc_rates, RNuptake/RNfixation/TRA and related soil rates can be calculated and observable on the finish date although they are not realized by a subsequent crop integration if the crop is deleted/terminated. State totals remain transition-based, but final-day rate output can be mistaken for realized flux.

findings.summary: Daily output is saved after current-day calc_rates but reads both states and rates through get_variable. States represent the just-integrated transition; rates represent the next transition. A single output row therefore intentionally mixes two temporal ownership levels. Rate variables in daily output must not be interpreted as fluxes already realized in that row's states.

Crop summary output is collected after crop.finalize; terminal output is collected after soil.finalize. State-based final metrics therefore use finalized states. No stale-state defect established, but summary and terminal channels have different component scopes by design.

TimedEventsDispatcher forbids duplicate dates only within one dispatcher, not across separate dispatchers or timed+state dispatchers. Multiple independent signals of the same physical type can therefore legitimately reach a handler on one day; handlers must be additive/idempotent as appropriate. AMEND02 and IRR01 demonstrate why this is an ownership contract.

Engine flushes published states before integration and published rates after integration/zerofy; components republish via prepared state/rate decorators. Crop deletion deregisters variables. This materially reduces stale-value reuse and no generic stale-kiosk defect was found.

After crop_finish and crop deletion, MLWB baseline retains the finished crop's rooting weights and _RDold while RD disappears from the kiosk. Fallow root-zone summaries can therefore remain based on the previous crop geometry until another crop starts. Repair marks root geometry for reset and rebuilds summary weights at default fallow RD on the next integration.

findings.summary: Organic amendment buffers concatenate each event and mineral amendment buffers now add after AMEND02. calc_rates snapshots all buffers into rates and resets placeholders immediately, giving one-rate-day ownership. No further same-day overwrite found.
_WLV_REALLOC/_WST_REALLOC are per-crop SimulationObject trait state and a new crop gets a new object after deletion. No cross-crop leakage of reallocation quota was established.

Crop cumulative GASST/MREST/CTRAT and soil cumulative water/N counters integrate realized previous-day rates. Daily instantaneous rate output remains prospective. No double accumulation was established, but comparing cumulative increments to same-row rates requires a one-boundary shift.

Rain, irrigation, surface storage, infiltration, evaporation and runoff are composed in one MLWB rate calculation and committed together in integrate. No additional overwrite/double-claim defect established in source audit.

REALLOC_LEAF/STEM_FRACTION, REALLOC_LEAF/STEM_RATE and REALLOC_EFFICIENCY are unconstrained Floats. Negative fractions/rates, fractions >1 or efficiencies outside [0,1] are accepted and can invert transfers or create more storage biomass than committed donor transfer. Hard physical bounds should be validated.

findings.summary: Maximum rooting depth is strongly validated against layer boundaries, and crop RDmax is min(RDMCR,RDMSOL). However basic positivity/order relationships among RDI, RDMCR and RDMSOL rely largely on input quality; rdmax=max(RDI,min(...)) can make RDI override nominal maxima if inconsistent parameters are supplied.

WOFOST81 selects DVS_Partitioning_N, whose implementation modifies root allocation with RFTRA and caps FR at 0.6. WOFOST72/73 use ordinary DVS partitioning in their standard crop classes. The N-specific class documentation instead describes N-stress/NPART effects and lists NNI, but NPART is commented out and NNI unused. This is not an accidental small code drift; it is an undocumented/contradictory 8.1 model divergence requiring maintainer decision.

WOFOST72/73 top-level GASST/MREST/CTRAT/CEVST accumulate daily rates without delt; WOFOST81 multiplies these top-level cumulatives by delt while many underlying organ/phenology integrations remain unscaled. This reinforces that WOFOST81's partial delt support is internally inconsistent rather than a complete variable-step modernization.
Across WOFOST72/73/81 the main PGASS→RFTRA→GASS→MRES→ASRC→CVF→DMI sequence and carbon-balance formulation are materially conserved. No unexplained 8.1 divergence established in this core.

The emerging-stage early return, phenology-before-organ integration, TAGP recomputation and crop-finish finalize pattern are inherited across versions. First/last-day temporal semantics are therefore broader PCSE/WOFOST architecture, not uniquely introduced by 8.1.
